title: U.S. House · Texas's 34th District
area: A South Texas district covering the Rio Grande Valley, including Brownsville and McAllen.

context.text: Rep. Vicente Gonzalez Jr. is the incumbent under Texas's 2026 congressional map. Eric Flores won the Republican nomination.

summary.text: Vicente Gonzalez Jr. is the incumbent U.S. Representative for South Texas's 34th District. He is an attorney who has served on the House Financial Services Committee throughout his tenure and chairs the Congressional Oil and Gas Caucus.

background.text: Born in Corpus Christi, Texas; earned an associate degree in banking and finance from Del Mar College, a bachelor's degree in business aviation from Embry-Riddle University, and a law degree from Texas Wesleyan University School of Law.
Worked as an attorney in private practice beginning in 1997.
Has served on the House Committee on Financial Services in every Congress since being elected in 2016; also previously served on the Committee on Foreign Affairs.

priorities.text: Chairs the Congressional Oil and Gas Caucus and supports an "all-the-above" energy approach.
priorities.quote: Congressman Gonzalez supports an all-the-above approach to energy and understands the importance of American energy not only to power our cars and homes, but also as a national security issue and a job creator.

priorities.text: Supports agricultural research, trade assistance, and crop insurance and disaster assistance programs for South Texas farmers and ranchers.
Says he works to lower health care costs and expand coverage, particularly for South Texas's uninsured and underinsured population.

positions.summary: Says he works to develop ideas that lower health care costs and provide better coverage, citing South Texas's large uninsured population.
Supports reducing barriers to the workforce, including lowering education costs and increasing access to childcare.
Supports an "all-the-above" energy approach that includes continued oil and gas production alongside other energy sources, rather than a faster transition away from fossil fuels.
positions.quote: Congressman Gonzalez supports an all-the-above approach to energy

record.text: Assigned to the House Committee on Financial Services in the 2025-2026 (119th) Congress.
Chairs the Congressional Oil and Gas Caucus.

summary.text: Eric Flores is an attorney and U.S. Army veteran who previously served as an assistant U.S. Attorney for the Southern District of Texas.

background.text: Earned a bachelor's degree from the University of Texas at Austin and a J.D. from Texas Southern University.
Served in the U.S. Army and the Texas Army National Guard.
Previously served as an assistant U.S. Attorney for the Southern District of Texas.

priorities.text: Says he supports securing the border and law enforcement.
Says he will defend the Second Amendment and advocate for veterans and U.S. energy independence.
Says he will support President Trump's agenda.

positions.summary: Campaign platform calls for securing the border.
Campaign platform calls for defending the Second Amendment.

summary.text: Eddie Espinoza is a U.S. Army veteran and retired Texas public school teacher of 26 years running as the Green Party nominee, with a platform focused on the environment.

background.text: Served in the U.S. Army from 1989 to 1991, including during Operation Desert Storm.
Earned a bachelor's degree from the University of Texas-Pan American in 1994.
Taught in Texas public schools for 26 years.

priorities.text: Supports plugging and decommissioning idle oil and gas wells he says are contaminating water sources.
Supports banning fracking and stopping new fossil-fuel infrastructure, including proposed LNG export terminals on the Gulf Coast.

positions.summary: Supports banning fracking, halting new fossil-fuel infrastructure, and decarbonizing the Texas economy.
positions.quote: Let's ban fracking and stop the expansion of new fossil fuels infrastructure and projects, including proposed LNG export terminals along the Gulf coast. Decarbonize the Texas economy, and make it more resilient to global warming.

summary.text: Chris Royal is a retired teacher and attorney running as the Libertarian Party nominee, with a platform emphasizing enforcement of existing immigration law.

background.text: Earned a J.D. from the Kansas City School of Law in 1990 after military service including the 1st Infantry Division and a stint at the Pentagon.
Worked in the legal and title businesses and as a teacher in the Rio Grande Valley before retiring.

priorities.text: Says immigration laws already on the books should be enforced.
priorities.quote: If elected, I vote to execute the laws on the books with respect to illegal border crossings.

positions.summary: Says he supports enforcing existing immigration laws regarding illegal border crossings.
positions.quote: If elected, I vote to execute the laws on the books with respect to illegal border crossings.
